objective: Build event flows from the Argo Events components: EventSource types (webhook, S3, Kafka, calendar, resource and more), the EventBus (NATS/JetStream), Sensors with dependencies, filters and triggers, and trigger parameterization
secondaryObjectives: Argo Events fundamentals: event-driven automation for Kubernetes and how it connects external systems to Workflows and other resources

sources.cite: Linux Foundation, Certified Argo Project Associate (CAPA) exam page: Argo Workflows 36%, Argo CD 34%, Argo Rollouts 18%, Argo Events 12%
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch of the Linux Foundation's page (last modified 2026-05-06). Its Argo Workflows topics are workflow fundamentals, artifacts, templates, the workflow spec, DAGs ('Work with DAG (Directed-Acyclic Graphs)') and data processing jobs; it does not mention retries or exit handlers. A study page (kube-dojo.github.io/k8s/capa, same weights) lists retryStrategy, backoff and exit handlers as study topics. The objective wording is the course seed's. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's argo-nightly-dag-region-failure (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: a dependency's data filter (path, type, comparator, value; string values are evaluated as regular expressions) decides whether an event is valid for the dependency.

Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: trigger parameters read a value from an event dependency's data (src dependencyName and dataKey) and write it to a field of the triggered resource (dest), such as a workflow argument.

Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: the JetStream EventBus runs as a StatefulSet with 3 replicas in the simplest example, with optional persistence (storage class, size); NATS Streaming reached end-of-life in June 2023 in favor of JetStream.

The company, the bucket, the workflows and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You run the data platform at Fernway Labs, a fictional genomics lab. Sequencers upload results to an S3-compatible bucket; an Argo Events S3 EventSource sends each upload to a Sensor that starts an Argo Workflow to process the sample. Overnight the pipeline started 4,000 workflows for 60 samples and the cluster queue is full.
handover: EventSource sequencer-bucket: S3 notifications for every object created in the results/ prefix.
Sensor sample-processor: one dependency on sequencer-bucket, no filters, one Argo Workflow trigger with the workflow's sample parameter hard-coded to 'latest'.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the map shows each component and its status in words.
Move on a check-in at a time. A decision comes to you at each check-in; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

filterPrompt.title: The Sensor fires on every part file
filterPrompt.context: Only the final results.json means a sample is complete. You can change the Sensor's dependency or the workflow.

choices.label: Add a filter on the dependency so only object keys ending in /results.json trigger, and delete the pending duplicate workflows

effects.log: The Sensor now fires once per sample.

choices.feedback: Filters on the dependency decide which events trigger; the duplicates never start.

choices.label: Leave the Sensor and add a first step to the workflow that exits if the key is not results.json

effects.log: Each workflow now exits early for part files.

choices.feedback: It works, but 60 workflows a sample still start and each takes a pod; the filter belongs in the Sensor.

choices.label: Delete the EventSource until the weekend and process samples by hand
choices.feedback: Removing the source stops the storm and every real sample with it; the lab's results go unprocessed.

paramPrompt.title: Every workflow processed 'latest'
paramPrompt.context: The trigger's sample parameter is hard-coded to 'latest', so the workflows read whatever was uploaded last, not the sample that fired them.

choices.label: Add trigger parameters that copy the event's object key into the workflow's sample argument (src dependency, dataKey on the key)

effects.log: Each workflow now gets the key of the sample that fired it.

choices.feedback: Trigger parameterization maps fields of the event into the triggered resource.

choices.label: Make the workflow list the bucket and process every sample not yet processed

effects.log: The workflow now scans the bucket.

choices.feedback: It ends up processing everything, but two runs can pick the same sample, and the event's data is thrown away.

choices.label: Leave it: rerun 'latest' every hour from a CronWorkflow instead

effects.log: An hourly rerun of 'latest' is scheduled.

choices.feedback: Only the last upload of each hour is processed; the others are silently skipped.

durablePrompt.title: Events lost on an EventBus restart
durablePrompt.context: The EventBus is one NATS replica without persistence. When it restarts, events in flight are lost; two samples from the night never started.

choices.label: Move the EventBus to JetStream with three replicas and persistent storage, and re-send notifications for the two lost samples

effects.log: JetStream with three replicas and persistence; the two samples re-sent.

choices.feedback: A replicated, persistent bus keeps events through a pod restart; the lost samples are replayed from the bucket.

choices.label: Re-send the two lost samples and leave the EventBus as it is
choices.feedback: Today's gap is closed, but the next restart loses events again.

choices.label: Ignore it: a restart is rare and the samples will turn up
choices.feedback: The lost events never come back by themselves; two patients' samples stay unprocessed.

reflection.question: Write the change record for the lab's platform team: why 4,000 workflows started, how the Sensor and trigger were fixed, and how lost events are prevented.

parts.label: Sensor and trigger
parts.criteria: A filter on the dependency (results.json) and trigger parameters that pass the event's key.
parts.modelAnswer: The Sensor fired on all 60 part files a sample; a dependency filter now passes only results.json. The trigger copies the event's object key into the workflow's sample argument.

parts.label: The EventBus
parts.criteria: Explains the single, non-persistent NATS replica, the JetStream change and the replayed samples.
parts.modelAnswer: One NATS replica without persistence lost events on restart. The bus is now JetStream with three replicas and storage, and the two lost samples were re-sent.

scoring.modelReasoning: An EventSource turns external events into the EventBus; a Sensor's dependencies, filtered by event data, decide which events trigger; and trigger parameters map the event's fields into the triggered workflow. Filter at the dependency, not in each workflow, and never drop the source to stop a storm. Pass the event's object key, not a fixed 'latest'. The EventBus carries every event: a single, non-persistent replica loses events on restart, so use a replicated, persistent JetStream bus and replay what was lost.
